mechaber.he:

יהיה שלחנו ערוך ומטה מוצעת יפה ומפה פרוסה כמו בסעודת הלילה ויברך על היין בורא פרי הגפן והוא נקרא קידושא רבה ואח"כ יטול ידיו (וע"ל סי' רע"א סעיף י"ב בהג"ה) ויבצע על לחם משנה כמו בלילה ויסעוד וגם זה הקידוש צריך שיהיה במקום סעודה ושלא יטעום קודם לו כלום כמו בקידוש הלילה ומיהו לשתות מים בבקר קודם תפלה מותר מפני שעדיין לא חל עליו חובת קידוש: הגה וע"ל כל דיני קידוש סי' רע"א רע"ב רע"ג:
mechaber.en:
The Sequence of the Shabbos Morning Meal, 2 Seifim: The table should be set, the couch on which one eats should be spread in an attractive manner, and
a cloth spread over the bread, as was done for the night meal. One should bless the wine with Borei Pri HaGafen, which is called Kiddusha Rabbah. Afterwards, one should wash his hands , breaks the two loaves of bread (Lechem Mishneh) like at night, and then feasts. This kiddush must also be in the location of the meal, and one may not taste or eat at all prior to it, like with the night time kiddush. And if one drinks water in the morning before praying, it is permitted, because the obligation of kiddush does not yet apply to him. ((see Siman 271, Seif 12 in the Rama) Rema: See above for all the laws of kiddush, Siman 271, 272, 273.) ויבצע על לחם משנה כמו בלילה ויסעוד וגם זה הקידוש צריך שיהיה במקום סעודה ושלא יטעום קודם לו כלום כמו בקידוש הלילה ומיהו לשתות מים בבקר קודם תפלה מותר מפני שעדיין לא חל עליו חובת קידוש: הגה וע"ל כל דיני קידוש סי' רע"א רע"ב רע"ג:

Magen Avraham siman 302 wrote that if the bed stands in a room one passes through and there is disgrace, it is permitted to spread it because it is for Shabbat need — therefore. And ostensibly since it is possible with spreading a sheet there is not so much disgrace; nevertheless Rokeach siman 55 wrote they spread ten sheets so that if he needs he may sit on one of them, see there. Eliyahu Rabbah paragraph 1; and likewise Maharam Tirol paragraph 6 that whatever one does for honor of the day is permitted and is forbidden only if done for weekday use, see there. And see further below siman 302 paragraph 23:

levushei_serad.en: Taz s.k. 1. And here there is a blessing that is not needed — meaning that per the law it is fitting for the one who brings forth food to bless first; and if one need not bless on beer because bread exempts all kinds of beverages except wine, as explained in siman 174 seif 1 and seif 7 — if so, when one blesses on beer first he causes a blessing that is not needed. Granted in the Temple on wine — even though by law the one who brings forth food precedes, as explained in siman 211 seif 4 — nevertheless because of kiddush they precede the wine; but here where there is no such reason, why precede the beer? And see Peri Megadim there:

עסי' רע"ג סעיף ה' ר"ל כיון דאין לו פת האיך יצא ידי קידוש הא אין קידוש אלא במ"ס ול"ל ששתה כוס שכר כמ"ש הגאונים בסי' רע"ג אם שתה כוס יין ז"א דהא כ' מ"א בסי' רע"ג ס"ק י"א דבשכר אפי' הוא חמר מדינה לא יצא ידי קידוש במ"ס וצ"ל דאכל מיני תרגומא דיוצאים בהם כמ"ש מ"א שם:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(א) (s.k. 2) This is reward — meaning in siman 272 Beit Yosef: Beit Yosef disputes whether at night Kiddush one sanctifies on beer if it is chamar medinah; but here for Kiddush of the day it is unspecified that they sanctify on it as if there is no dispute. Regarding morning Kiddush they rely, etc., so there will be a change and recognition — for if he sanctifies on bread and blesses Hamotzi it is not recognizable that it is because of Kiddush, for in every meal one blesses Hamotzi; unlike when he blesses on beer before the meal it is recognizable that it is because of Kiddush, for it is not his way to drink before Hamotzi; unlike at night where even on bread there is recognition because at night one says the Kiddush blessing — therefore it is better to decide to sanctify on bread than to sanctify on beer. Even if he did not bless on bread — meaning for example he did not eat bread — for certainly if he ate bread he fulfills Kiddush in any case, whether with beer or bread, as Magen Avraham wrote end of siman 272:

(ב) Regarding siman 272 seif 5 — meaning since he has no bread how can he fulfill Kiddush? For there is no Kiddush except in a place of a meal; and it is not necessary that he drank a cup of beer as the Geonim wrote in siman 272 — if he drank a cup of wine, that is fine; for Magen Avraham wrote in siman 272 s.k. 11 that on beer even if it is chamar medinah he does not fulfill Kiddush in a place of a meal; and it must be said that he ate types of food with which one fulfills, as Magen Avraham wrote there:
